name: Hijuk
world_status: a description exists but is not accessible

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3 languoid page hiju1238 reference list (4 entries) + Wikipedia (en/fr) Hijuk pages
sources.note: Bibliographic check only: Glottolog lists Bassong 2007, Bradley 1992, Connell 2007, Moseley 2010; Wikipedia bibliographies cite only Bradley 1992 and Ethnologue. CrossRef, Semantic Scholar, HAL, theses.fr and archive.org full-text return no linguistic work on Hijuk.

sources.citation: Boyd, Virginia Lee. 2015. The phonological systems of the Mbam languages of Cameroon with a focus on vowels and vowel harmony. LOT dissertation 410. Utrecht: LOT.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on Hijuk prosody; pp. 2-3 explicitly exclude Hijuk from the study ('Due to this similarity to Basaa, Hijuk was not included in this study'), citing Boone/Bradley 1992 for the 87% Basaa figure.

sources.citation: Bradley, David P. 1992. Hijuk survey report. Yaoundé: SIL / Ministry of Higher Education, Computer Services and Scientific Research. 8 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. Rapid-appraisal sociolinguistic survey: location, ~400 speakers, lexicostatistics (87% similarity with Basaa, 31% with Bafia), language use, translation-need recommendation. No phonology of any kind.

sources.citation: Bassong, Paul Roger. 2007. Noun morphology and the internal structure of the nominal construction in Hijuk. MA thesis, Université de Yaoundé I.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: print only (no digital copy found when the work was looked up); access check: not located online or in the libraries checked
sources.note: The only descriptive linguistic work on Hijuk known to Glottolog; Yaoundé I MA theses on morphology normally open with a phonological overview (segment inventory, tones, syllable structure) that would state whether the language is tonal and whether any stress/accent is noted.

sources.citation: SIL Cameroon 1992 Hijuk 183-item survey wordlist (collected by Boone, Bradley & Grant, Feb-Mar 1992; unpublished, referenced in Bradley 1992 p.4)
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Tone-marked survey wordlist underlying the 87% Basaa figure; unpublished SIL Cameroon archive material, the only phonetic transcription of Hijuk known to exist besides ALCAM.

sources.citation: Dieu, Michel & Patrick Renaud (eds.). 1983. Atlas linguistique du Cameroun (ALCAM). Paris: ACCT; Yaoundé: CERDOTOLA/DGRST. [entry 560 Hijuk] (and Bikoi 2012 revised ALCAM)
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: print only (no digital copy found when the work was looked up)
sources.note: ALCAM classified Hijuk [560] on lexical and morphological correspondences and holds the only other primary data (wordlist); its inventory notes sometimes mark tone; would at least confirm tonal status.

sources.citation: Connell, Bruce. 2007. Endangered Languages in Central Africa. In Brenzinger (ed.), Language Diversity Endangered, 163-178. Berlin: Mouton de Gruyter.
